subject: Music Production
title: J Dilla's Sampling Philosophy
description: A fast breakdown of J Dilla's Sampling Philosophy for builders.

hook.text: J Dilla transformed samples so completely that listeners could rarely identify the original source.

buildup.text: He chopped, pitched, filtered, and rearranged samples into entirely new melodies and grooves.

discovery.text: His album 'Donuts' used over forty samples per track, blended so seamlessly they sounded original.

twist.text: Dilla made 'Donuts' from his hospital bed while battling a rare blood disease, finishing it days before his death.

climax.text: His work proved sampling could be as original and personal as composing from scratch.

punchline.text: He made other people's music sound entirely his own.

quiz.question: What made J Dilla's sampling distinctive?
options: He transformed samples so completely they sounded original
He used no effects on his samples
